1. Introduction
With the well development in ﬁnancial industry,
market starts to catch people’s eyes, not only by
the diversiﬁed investing choices ranging from bonds
and stocks, to futures and options, but also by the
general ”high-risk, high-reward” mindset prompt-
ing people to put money in ﬁnancial market. What
we always show concerns for, is nothing but two
terms, risk, and return. People are interested in
reducing risk at a given level of return since there
is no way having both high return and low risk.
Many researchers have been studying on this issue,
and the most pioneering one is Harry Markowitz’s
Modern Portfolio Theory developed in 1952, which
is the cornerstone of investment portfolio manage-
ment. Markowitz’s MPT is one of the most widely-
used structure in terms of portfolio construction,
which aims at ”maximum the return at the given
risk”. In contrast to that, ﬁfty years later, E. Robert
Fernholz’s Stochastic Portfolio Theory , as opposed
to the normative assumption served as the basis of
earlier modern portfolio theory, is consistent with
the observable characteristics of actual portfolios
and markets.
In this paper, you will see ﬁrst some basic theo-
ries of Markowitz’s MPT and Fernholz’s SPT. Next
we step across to application side, trying to ﬁgure
out under four basic models based on Markowitz Ef-
ﬁcient Frontier, including Markowitz Model , Con-
stant Correlation Model , Single Index Model , and
Multi-Factor Model, what portfolios will be selected
and how do these portfolios perform in real world.
Here we also involve Universal Portfolio Algorithm
by Thomas M. Cover to select portfolios as compar-
ison. In addition, each portfolio’s Value at Risk, Ex-
pected Shortfall and corresponding Bootstrap conﬁ-
dence interval for risk management will be evalu-
ated. Finally, by utilizing factor analysis and time
series model, we could predict future performance
of our four models.

higher return must accept higher risk, but diﬀerent
people may have their own risk toleration, which
lead to diﬀerent investment strategies, forming the
so-called Eﬃcient Frontier. Under the model, we

In this section we will go further into return predic-

sis. Primarily, we split our calculated log return into

In order to see which factors are signiﬁcantly con-

The result only choose Volume, Market Return and
Risk-free Rate as signiﬁcant factors.
One interesting thing about stock return is that
the residuals do not satisfy the general assumptions
of multivariate regression analysis. Generally we as-
sume that the residuals follow independent identi-
cally distributedN (0,σ 2), thus after ﬁtting regres-
sion model we are done with predicting process,
since the predicted value is just the ﬁtted value due
to zero-mean residuals. While this is not the case
here. Financial data have the so-called cluster ef-
fect that observations do not follow linear pattern
but rather tend to cluster due to heteroskedasticity.
Therefore, the conclusions and predicted value one
can draw from the model will not be reliable, which
motivate us to use the GARCH model to capture
the volatility variations. Based on the log-return
residuals of the four models and their ACF and
PACF plots performance, we have selected diﬀerent
ARMA+GARCH model respectively.
Comparing prediction result, Multi-Factor Model
has adjusted R-squared 0.2503, so the best we can
do is merely to explain 25.03% of the variation in
the calculated log return.

4. Conclusion
Return and risk trade-oﬀ is an eternal theme, that
investors always think about. In this article are are
focusing on dealing with the relationship between
them, by utilizing most famous Markowitz’s Mod-
ern Portfolio Theory. In addition to that, under four
models, Markowitz Model, Constant Correlation
Model, Single Index Model and Multi-factor Model,
we develop eﬃcient investment strategy, construct
portfolios, thereby seize the volatility structure and
predict future performance. All in all, Multi-factor
Model seems to be the outstanding one in both risk
management and return prediction, however, the ﬁ-

As you may wonder, why cannot the models cap-

believe that ﬁnancial market has more variability
beyond the scope of the whole bunch of fundamen-

complex model we could do better.

Hidden Order in Trades Predicts the Size of Price Moves

Hidden Order in Trades Predicts the Size of PriceMoves
November 2025

Abstract
Financial markets exhibit an apparent paradox: while directional price movements remain
largely unpredictable—consistent with weak-form efficiency—themagnitudeof price changes
displays systematic structure. Here we demonstrate that real-time order-flow entropy, com-
puted from a 15-state Markov transition matrix at second resolution, predicts the magnitude
of intraday returns without providing directional information. Analysis of 38.5 million SPY
trades over 36 trading days reveals that conditioning on entropy below the 5th percentile
increases subsequent 5-minute absolute returns by a factor of 2.89 (t= 12.41,p <10 −4),
while directional accuracy remains at 45.0%—statistically indistinguishable from chance
(p= 0.12). This decoupling arises from a fundamental symmetry: entropy is invariant
under sign permutation, detecting thepresenceof informed trading without revealing its
direction. Walk-forward validation across five non-overlapping test periods confirms out-of-
sample predictability, and label-permutation placebo tests yieldz= 14.4against the null.
These findings suggest that information-theoretic measures may serve as volatility state
variables in market microstructure, though the limited sample (36 days, single instrument)
requires extended validation.
arXiv:2512.15720v1  [q-fin.TR]  2 Dec 2025

The efficient market hypothesis posits that asset prices fully reflect available information,
rendering future price movements unpredictable[1]. Empirical tests have largely confirmed this
prediction fordirectionalforecasting: momentum[2] and mean-reversion[3] effects, while statis-
tically significant, explain only a small fraction of return variance. Yet pricemagnitude—how
far prices move, irrespective of direction—represents a distinct forecasting target that need not
obey the same constraints.
This distinction has theoretical grounding in market microstructure theory. In the Kyle[4]
and Glosten-Milgrom[5] frameworks, informed traders possessing private information generate
persistent order flow that moves prices toward fundamental values. The critical observation is
that this persistence creates statistical structure in the transaction sequence—a departure from
randomness that information-theoretic measures can detect—without revealing thesignof the
private information. An informed buyer generates the same entropy signature as an informed
seller: both produce order flow that is more predictable than the noise-trader baseline.
We formalize this insight by constructing a Time-Dependent Entropy measure from tick-
level market data. At each second, the market occupies one of 15 discrete states defined by
the cross-product of price-change sign ({−1,0,+1}) and volume quintile ({1,2,3,4,5}). The
transition matrix ˆPt is estimated over a rolling 120-second window, and entropy is computed as
the stationary-weighted average of row entropies, normalized to[0,1]:

Empirical Results
We tested these predictions using 38,509,593 SPY trades from October 1 to November 19, 2025
(36 trading days), aggregated to second-resolution bars (828,907 observations). Figure 1 displays
the central finding: absolute 5-minute returns increase monotonically as entropy decreases. The
lowest quintile exhibits mean absolute returns of 8.14 bps versus 3.75 bps in the highest quintile
(ratio: 2.17). Conditioning on entropy below the 5th percentile yields 15.3 bps—a factor of 2.89
above the unconditional mean (t= 12.41,p <10 −4).

Limitations and Interpretation
Several constraints limit interpretation. First, the sample comprises only 36 trading days of a
single instrument—far shorter than standard validation periods in quantitative finance. Second,
October 29 alone contributed 38.5% of profits, raising concentration concerns. Third, execution
assumptions (immediate fills, fixed costs) may not hold at scale. Fourth, VIX remained in the
14–22 range throughout; behavior during high-volatility regimes is unknown.
Despite these caveats, the theoretical framework and empirical consistency suggest that
order-flow entropy may constitute a useful state variable for intraday volatility timing. The
finding that entropy predicts magnitude but not direction is not merely an empirical curiosity—
it follows necessarily from the mathematical structure of entropy itself, specifically its invariance
under label permutation. This invariance implies that any information-theoretic measure with
this symmetry property will exhibit the same decoupling.
Fromtheperspectiveofmarketefficiency, theseresultsdonotcontradictweak-formefficiency.
Predictingthata large move will occur is categorically different from predictingwhich direction
it will go. The former is consistent with informed traders acting on private information; the
latter would require access to that information’s sign. Our findings suggest that microstructure
entropy reveals theactivityof informed traders without revealing theirintent.
Extended validation—longer time series, multiple instruments, live execution—is required
before practical application. The present analysis establishes the theoretical basis for entropy-
based magnitude prediction and provides preliminary empirical support within a limited sample.

    """Amihud illiquidity shock: a spike in price impact demands a premium.

    Mechanism: when a name's price impact per dollar traded jumps relative to
    its own recent norm, liquidity providers demand compensation to hold it —
    subsequent returns are higher until impact normalises (Amihud 2002)."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns, ts_mean
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    @register_factor
    class AmihudShock(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "amihud_shock"
        name = "Amihud illiquidity shock"
        category = "microstructure"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of short-run Amihud price impact "
            "(5-bar mean of |return| per unit dollar volume) relative to its "
            "own 60-bar level: long names whose impact just spiked."
        )
        window_length = 60
        inputs = ["close", "volume"]
        prediction_horizon = 6      # bars over which the liquidity premium accrues
        suggested_horizons = [3, 6, 12]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            close = data["close"]
            ret = returns(data)
            dollar = (close * data["volume"]).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            illiq = ret.abs() / dollar            # Amihud (2002) price impact
            base = ts_mean(illiq, 60).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            return rank(ts_mean(illiq, 5) / base)

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""

        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _loo_group_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, groups: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal row-wise leave-one-out group mean, preserving the input panel."""
    valid = values.notna() & groups.notna()
    filled = values.where(valid, 0.0)
    counts = valid.astype(float).groupby(groups, axis=1).transform("sum")
    totals = filled.groupby(groups, axis=1).transform("sum")
    denominator = (counts - valid.astype(float)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (totals - filled) / denominator


def _liquidity_innovation(illiq: pd.DataFrame, short_window: int, long_window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Standardized trailing innovation in log range-per-volume liquidity stress."""
    log_illiq = np.log1p(illiq.clip(lower=0.0))
    baseline = log_illiq.rolling(long_window, min_periods=long_window).mean()
    dispersion = log_illiq.rolling(long_window, min_periods=long_window).std()
    recent = log_illiq.rolling(short_window, min_periods=short_window).mean()
    return (recent - baseline) / dispersion.replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class LiquidityResilienceSynchronyBreakHazard(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks isolated liquidity shocks by downside hazard versus close-location repair."""

    factor_id = "liquidity_resilience_synchrony_break_hazard"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Liquidity Synchrony-Break Hazard"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of a name-specific range-per-volume liquidity "
        "innovation after removing its leave-one-out sector component, signed "
        "by close location and amplified when recent ranges are expanding."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        reference_price = prior_close.where(prior_close.notna(), close)
        true_range = pd.concat(
            [
                (high - low).abs(),
                (high - reference_price).abs(),
                (low - reference_price).abs(),
            ],
            axis=0,
        ).groupby(level=0).max()
        normalized_range = true_range / reference_price.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        illiquidity = normalized_range / volume.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)

        innovation = _liquidity_innovation(illiquidity, 3, 40)
        sector_component = _loo_group_mean(innovation, sector)
        idiosyncratic_shock = innovation - sector_component

        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((close - low) / bar_range).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        close_repair = 2.0 * close_location - 1.0

        short_range = normalized_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        long_range = normalized_range.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        range_expansion = short_range / long_range.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        expansion_scale = 1.0 + range_expansion.clip(lower=-0.75, upper=2.0)

        score = idiosyncratic_shock * close_repair * expansion_scale
        return rank(score).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _ewm_arrival_masses(
    signed_arrival: pd.DataFrame,
    halflife: float,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute causal exponentially weighted positive, negative, and total flow masses."""
    positive = signed_arrival.clip(lower=0.0)
    negative = (-signed_arrival.clip(upper=0.0))
    unsigned = signed_arrival.abs()
    return (
        positive.ewm(halflife=halflife, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean(),
        negative.ewm(halflife=halflife, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean(),
        unsigned.ewm(halflife=halflife, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean(),
    )


def _directional_persistence(
    signed_arrival: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal path-direction ratio: net signed arrival divided by total arrival."""
    net_mass = signed_arrival.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    gross_mass = signed_arrival.abs().rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    return net_mass / gross_mass.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _alternation_penalty(
    signed_arrival: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing weighted sign-flip rate, high when directional participation alternates."""
    direction = np.sign(signed_arrival)
    prior_direction = direction.shift(1)
    valid_pair = (direction != 0.0) & (prior_direction != 0.0)
    flips = ((direction * prior_direction) < 0.0).where(valid_pair, np.nan).astype(float)
    weights = signed_arrival.abs()
    pair_weight = (weights * weights.shift(1)).pow(0.5).where(valid_pair, np.nan)
    weighted_flips = (flips * pair_weight).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    total_weight = pair_weight.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    return weighted_flips / total_weight.replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class VolumeArrivalAsymmetryInformationPersistence(BaseFactor):
    """Directional, persistent volume arrivals adjusted for alternation and liquidity shocks."""

    factor_id = "volume_arrival_asymmetry_information_persistence"
    name = "Directional Volume-Arrival Information Score"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks persistent directional volume-surprise arrivals measured by close "
        "location in range, while penalizing sign alternation and abnormal "
        "range-per-volume dislocations associated with liquidity shocks."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)

        safe_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
        log_volume = np.log1p(safe_volume)
        volume_baseline = log_volume.rolling(60, min_periods=20).mean()
        volume_scale = log_volume.rolling(60, min_periods=20).std()
        volume_surprise = (log_volume - volume_baseline) / volume_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        volume_surprise = volume_surprise.clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

        bar_range = (high - low).where((high - low) > 0.0)
        close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
        close_location = close_location.fillna(0.0)

        signed_arrival = volume_surprise * close_location
        positive_mass, negative_mass, unsigned_mass = _ewm_arrival_masses(
            signed_arrival,
            5.0,
        )
        arrival_asymmetry = (positive_mass - negative_mass) / unsigned_mass.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        persistence = _directional_persistence(signed_arrival, 12)
        alternation = _alternation_penalty(signed_arrival, 12)

        normalized_range = bar_range / close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        range_per_volume = normalized_range / np.sqrt(safe_volume).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        shock_center = range_per_volume.rolling(60, min_periods=20).median()
        shock_dispersion = range_per_volume.rolling(60, min_periods=20).std()
        shock_zscore = (range_per_volume - shock_center) / shock_dispersion.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        liquidity_shock_penalty = shock_zscore.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)

        raw_score = (
            arrival_asymmetry.fillna(0.0)
            * persistence.abs().fillna(0.0)
            * (1.0 - alternation.fillna(1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0))
            / (1.0 + liquidity_shock_penalty)
        )
        return rank(raw_score).fillna(0.5)

    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _transition_entropy(states: pd.DataFrame, window: int, n_states: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing Shannon entropy of one-step Markov transition outcomes.

    A transition is encoded as previous_state * n_states + current_state.  Each
    rolling count is trailing-only, so the entropy available on a date uses no
    observations after that date.  Entropy is normalized to [0, 1], where a
    low value means that the joint return/volume path repeatedly follows a
    small, predictable set of transitions.
    """
    previous = states.shift(1)
    transition = previous * float(n_states) + states
    valid = previous.notna() & states.notna()
    transition = transition.where(valid)

    counts = []
    for transition_id in range(n_states * n_states):
        indicator = (transition == float(transition_id)).astype(float)
        indicator = indicator.where(valid, np.nan)
        counts.append(indicator.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum())

    total = pd.concat(counts, axis=0, keys=range(n_states * n_states)).groupby(level=1).sum()
    # The concat/groupby construction retains the original timestamp-column
    # panel for each transition count; reconstruct probabilities explicitly.
    entropy = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=states.index, columns=states.columns)
    for count in counts:
        probability = count / total.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        entropy = entropy - probability.where(probability > 0.0, 1.0).apply(np.log) * probability.fillna(0.0)

    return entropy / np.log(float(n_states * n_states))


def _markov_transition_entropy(states: pd.DataFrame, window: int, n_states: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Panel-safe trailing transition entropy without cross-ticker aggregation."""
    previous = states.shift(1)
    valid = previous.notna() & states.notna()
    transition = (previous * float(n_states) + states).where(valid)

    total = valid.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    entropy = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=states.index, columns=states.columns)
    for transition_id in range(n_states * n_states):
        count = (transition == float(transition_id)).astype(float)
        count = count.where(valid, np.nan).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
        probability = count / total.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        entropy = entropy - probability.where(probability > 0.0, 1.0).apply(np.log) * probability.fillna(0.0)

    return entropy / np.log(float(n_states * n_states))


@register_factor
class CompressedFlowReleaseDirectionalPressure(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks persistent pressure when predictable flow and range compression align."""

    factor_id = "compressed_flow_release_directional_pressure"
    name = "Compressed Flow Release Pressure"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Rolling Markov-transition entropy of return-sign and relative-volume "
        "states identifies predictable execution paths; cross-sectionally rank "
        "persistent signed pressure only when entropy and intraday range are "
        "both unusually compressed."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan).ffill()
        high = data["high"].replace(0.0, np.nan).ffill()
        low = data["low"].replace(0.0, np.nan).ffill()
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        volume_base = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_volume = (volume / volume_base).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(1.0)

        # Three return-sign states and three volume states yield nine joint
        # states.  The thresholds deliberately use broad buckets so ordinary
        # daily noise does not create artificial transition complexity.
        sign_state = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(ret.to_numpy() > 0.0, 2.0, np.where(ret.to_numpy() < 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=ret.columns,
        )
        volume_state = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(
                relative_volume.to_numpy() < 0.75,
                0.0,
                np.where(relative_volume.to_numpy() > 1.25, 2.0, 1.0),
            ),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=ret.columns,
        )
        joint_state = sign_state * 3.0 + volume_state
        entropy = _markov_transition_entropy(joint_state, 20, 9)

        entropy_cutoff = entropy.rolling(60, min_periods=30).quantile(0.35)
        low_entropy = entropy <= entropy_cutoff

        true_range = ((high - low) / close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        short_range = true_range.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        normal_range = true_range.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        range_ratio = short_range / normal_range
        compressed_range = range_ratio <= 0.75

        # Relative-volume-weighted returns retain direction while emphasizing
        # repeated execution on active days.  The trailing sum is a causal
        # approximation to latent accumulated buy/sell pressure.
        pressure = (ret * relative_volume.clip(lower=0.25, upper=3.0)).rolling(
            8, min_periods=5
        ).sum()
        regime = low_entropy & compressed_range & pressure.notna()
        ranked_pressure = rank(pressure.where(regime)) - 0.5

        return ranked_pressure.fillna(0.0).astype(float)

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _trailing_zscore(frame: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal trailing standardization with no use of future observations."""
    mean = frame.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    std = frame.rolling(window, min_periods=window).std()
    return (frame - mean) / std.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _complex_coherence_proxy(
    return_z: pd.DataFrame,
    volume_z: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing complex return-volume coherence using in-phase and lag channels.

    The contemporaneous product is the in-phase component.  The product of
    today's standardized return with yesterday's volume innovation is a
    one-bar quadrature proxy.  Both are normalized by trailing channel energy.
    """
    lagged_volume_z = volume_z.shift(1)

    in_phase = (return_z * volume_z).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    quadrature = (return_z * lagged_volume_z).rolling(
        window, min_periods=window
    ).mean()

    return_energy = (return_z * return_z).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    volume_energy = (lagged_volume_z * lagged_volume_z).rolling(
        window, min_periods=window
    ).mean()
    normalizer = np.sqrt(return_energy * volume_energy).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    coherence = np.sqrt(in_phase * in_phase + quadrature * quadrature) / normalizer
    return coherence.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)


@register_factor
class ReturnVolumePhaseLockingBreak(BaseFactor):
    """Scores reversals after return-volume phase locking abruptly breaks."""

    factor_id = "return_volume_phase_locking_break"
    name = "Return-Volume Phase-Locking Break"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional reversal score for names whose standardized signed "
        "returns and log-volume innovations recently exhibited strong complex "
        "coherence, then abruptly decoupled while the price remains directionally "
        "extended."
    )
    window_length = 100
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].where(data["volume"] > 0.0, np.nan)

        log_close = np.log(close)
        signed_return = log_close.diff()
        log_volume = np.log(volume)
        volume_innovation = log_volume - log_volume.shift(1)

        return_z = _trailing_zscore(signed_return, 20)
        volume_z = _trailing_zscore(volume_innovation, 20)
        coherence = _complex_coherence_proxy(return_z, volume_z, 30)

        # Coherence must have been elevated before the current collapse, rather
        # than merely low because the name has never had informed participation.
        prior_coherence = coherence.shift(1).rolling(5, min_periods=5).max()
        coherence_mean = coherence.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean()
        coherence_std = coherence.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=40).std()
        high_locking = (
            (prior_coherence - coherence_mean)
            / coherence_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0)

        collapse = (
            (prior_coherence - coherence)
            / coherence_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0)

        # A five-bar standardized price displacement supplies the impulse sign
        # and ensures that the decoupling occurs while price is still extended.
        impulse_return = signed_return.rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
        daily_volatility = signed_return.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
        extended_impulse = impulse_return / (
            np.sqrt(5.0) * daily_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        # Negative sign expresses the expected reversal opposite the completed
        # information-driven impulse.  Squared magnitude emphasizes materially
        # extended prices without changing the reversal direction.
        raw_signal = (
            -extended_impulse
            * extended_impulse.abs()
            * high_locking
            * collapse
        )

        return rank(raw_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0))

    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _robust_range_volume_residual(
    log_range: pd.DataFrame,
    log_volume: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal winsorized rolling regression residual of log range on log volume.

    Rolling medians and MADs define trailing robust clipping bounds.  The
    resulting rolling covariance slope is less sensitive to isolated news bars
    than an ordinary rolling least-squares slope, while using only information
    available at each timestamp.
    """
    min_obs = window

    x_median = log_volume.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).median()
    y_median = log_range.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).median()

    x_mad = (log_volume - x_median).abs().rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).median()
    y_mad = (log_range - y_median).abs().rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).median()

    x_scale = (1.4826 * x_mad).where(x_mad > 1.0e-8, 1.0e-8)
    y_scale = (1.4826 * y_mad).where(y_mad > 1.0e-8, 1.0e-8)

    x_lo = x_median - 3.0 * x_scale
    x_hi = x_median + 3.0 * x_scale
    y_lo = y_median - 3.0 * y_scale
    y_hi = y_median + 3.0 * y_scale

    x_robust = log_volume.clip(lower=x_lo, upper=x_hi, axis=None)
    y_robust = log_range.clip(lower=y_lo, upper=y_hi, axis=None)

    x_mean = x_robust.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    y_mean = y_robust.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    xy_mean = (x_robust * y_robust).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    xx_mean = (x_robust * x_robust).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean()

    covariance = xy_mean - x_mean * y_mean
    variance = xx_mean - x_mean * x_mean
    slope = covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    intercept = y_median - slope * x_median

    return log_range - (intercept + slope * log_volume)


@register_factor
class RangeVolumeElasticityThinningDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Directional pressure from range expansion unexplained by traded volume."""

    factor_id = "range_volume_elasticity_thinning_drift"
    name = "Liquidity-Thinning Impact Elasticity"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of close-location-signed range expansion that is "
        "unexplained by a robust trailing log-range versus log-volume slope and "
        "is accelerating versus its recent residual history."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].where(data["close"] > 0.0)
        high = data["high"].where(data["high"].notna(), close)
        low = data["low"].where(data["low"].notna(), close)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        bar_range = (high - low).abs()
        relative_range = bar_range / close
        log_range = np.log(relative_range.clip(lower=1.0e-8))
        log_volume = np.log1p(volume)

        residual = _robust_range_volume_residual(log_range, log_volume, 60)
        positive_residual = residual.clip(lower=0.0)

        prior_residual_mean = residual.shift(1).rolling(5, min_periods=3).mean()
        acceleration = (residual - prior_residual_mean).clip(lower=0.0)

        close_location = (
            (2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)

        pressure = close_location * positive_residual * acceleration
        return rank(pressure).fillna(0.5)

    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (

        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _trailing_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal trailing standardization, clipped to limit single-bar outliers."""
    mean = values.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    std = values.rolling(window, min_periods=window).std()
    zscore = (values - mean) / std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return zscore.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)


def _loo_sector_mean(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Leave-one-out sector mean requiring at least two valid peers."""
    valid_float = valid.astype(float)
    clean_values = values.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

    group_sums = clean_values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).sum().T
    group_counts = valid_float.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).sum().T

    expanded_sums = group_sums.reindex(columns=labels.to_numpy())
    expanded_counts = group_counts.reindex(columns=labels.to_numpy())
    expanded_sums.columns = values.columns
    expanded_counts.columns = values.columns

    peer_count = expanded_counts - valid_float
    peer_sum = expanded_sums - clean_values
    result = peer_sum / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return result.where(peer_count >= 2.0)

    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]

        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)

        sector_labels = data["sector"].iloc[0].astype(object)
        sector_labels = sector_labels.where(sector_labels.notna(), "__MISSING_SECTOR__")
        sector_labels.index = close.columns

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.clip(lower=0.0)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        range_z = _trailing_zscore(normalized_range, 20)
        volume_z = _trailing_zscore(log_volume, 20)

        range_event = (range_z > 0.75).astype(float).where(range_z.notna())
        volume_event = (volume_z > 0.75).astype(float).where(volume_z.notna())
        joint_event = ((range_z > 0.75) & (volume_z > 0.75)).astype(float)
        joint_event = joint_event.where(range_z.notna() & volume_z.notna())

        range_breadth = _loo_sector_mean(
            range_event, range_event.notna(), sector_labels
        )
        volume_breadth = _loo_sector_mean(
            volume_event, volume_event.notna(), sector_labels
        )
        joint_breadth = _loo_sector_mean(
            joint_event, joint_event.notna(), sector_labels
        )

        # The geometric component penalizes a sector where only one channel is
        # active; joint breadth further requires the same peers to show both.
        synchrony = np.sqrt((range_breadth * volume_breadth).clip(lower=0.0))
        synchrony = (synchrony * joint_breadth).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        peer_return = _loo_sector_mean(returns, returns.notna(), sector_labels)
        sector_impulse = peer_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        own_impulse = returns.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        shortfall = sector_impulse - own_impulse

        # A name that has already made an unusually large three-day move is a
        # poor relay candidate even if its direction differs from its sector.
        daily_volatility = returns.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
        own_move_z = own_impulse.abs() / (daily_volatility * np.sqrt(3.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        own_move_weight = 1.0 / (1.0 + own_move_z.clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0))

        raw_score = shortfall * synchrony * own_move_weight
        raw_score = raw_score.where(synchrony >= 0.15)

        ranked = raw_score.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return ranked.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0).astype(float)

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:

        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):

{"code":""""A stock that abruptly becomes a correlation bridge between otherwise separate sector or industry clusters is more likely being driven by broad ETF, macro, or risk-parity flow than by stock-specific information. When that bridge formation coincides with an unusually large sector-neutral return and abnormal volume, the move should partially reverse as cross-asset synchronization fades and idiosyncratic pricing reasserts itself. The hypothesis is falsified if bridge-score increases are instead followed by persistent same-direction residual returns after controlling for sector moves."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_neutral_returns(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, sector_labels: np.ndarray
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove each date's contemporaneous sector return using static labels."""
    neutral = ret.copy()
    for label in np.unique(sector_labels):
        members = sector_labels == label
        group_ret = ret.loc[:, members]
        neutral.loc[:, members] = group_ret.sub(group_ret.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    return neutral


def _rolling_cross_sector_bridge(
    residual_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    sector_labels: np.ndarray,
    window: int,
    min_observations: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal cross-community bridge score from trailing correlation graphs.

    For each stock and each external sector, the graph edge is the strongest
    positive correlation with any member of that sector.  A bridge has both
    strong and diversified edges across external sector communities.
    """
    n_time, n_assets = residual_ret.shape
    labels = np.asarray(sector_labels)
    unique_labels = np.unique(labels)
    n_groups = len(unique_labels)
    scores = np.full((n_time, n_assets), np.nan, dtype=float)

    # A meaningful entropy-based bridge needs at least two external communities.
    if n_groups < 3:
        return pd.DataFrame(scores, index=residual_ret.index, columns=residual_ret.columns)

    group_members = [np.flatnonzero(labels == label) for label in unique_labels]
    asset_group = np.searchsorted(unique_labels, labels)

    for end in range(min_observations - 1, n_time):
        start = max(0, end - window + 1)
        sample = residual_ret.iloc[start : end + 1]
        corr = sample.corr(min_periods=min_observations).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        np.fill_diagonal(corr, np.nan)

        # Rows are external communities, columns are candidate bridge stocks.
        edges = np.zeros((n_groups, n_assets), dtype=float)
        for group_number, members in enumerate(group_members):
            block = corr[:, members]
            finite_block = np.where(np.isfinite(block), block, -np.inf)
            strongest = finite_block.max(axis=1)
            strongest[~np.isfinite(strongest)] = 0.0
            edges[group_number] = np.maximum(strongest, 0.0)

        # Own-sector links are not cross-community bridge links.
        edges[asset_group, np.arange(n_assets)] = 0.0
        edge_sum = edges.sum(axis=0)
        valid = edge_sum > 0.0
        if not np.any(valid):
            scores[end] = 0.0
            continue

        weights = np.zeros_like(edges)
        weights[:, valid] = edges[:, valid] / edge_sum[valid]
        safe_weights = np.where(weights > 0.0, weights, 1.0)
        entropy = -(weights * np.log(safe_weights)).sum(axis=0)

        # There are n_groups - 1 possible external sectors for each asset.
        normalized_entropy = entropy / np.log(float(n_groups - 1))
        top_two_strength = np.partition(edges, n_groups - 2, axis=0)[-2:].mean(axis=0)
        score = normalized_entropy * top_two_strength
        score[~valid] = 0.0
        scores[end] = score

    return pd.DataFrame(scores, index=residual_ret.index, columns=residual_ret.columns)


def _trailing_zscore(value: pd.DataFrame, window: int, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing-only z-score with stable handling for constant histories."""
    mean = value.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean()
    std = value.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (value - mean) / std


@register_factor
class CorrelationBridgeForcedFlowReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Fade sector-neutral moves accompanied by new cross-sector correlation bridges."""

    factor_id = "correlation_bridge_forcedflow_reversal"
    name = "Correlation-Bridge Forced-Flow Reversal"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Builds a trailing sector-neutral correlation graph and identifies stocks "
        "whose strongest positive links become diversified across external sectors. "
        "It fades recent residual returns only when bridge creation and relative "
        "volume are simultaneously abnormal."
    )
    window_length = 110
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)

        # Sector is static in this feed; using the first available panel row is
        # causal and avoids deriving labels from later market observations.
        sector_row = data["sector"].iloc[0].fillna("Unknown").astype(str)
        sector_labels = sector_row.reindex(close.columns).fillna("Unknown").to_numpy()

        valid_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        ret = valid_close.pct_change(fill_method=None).clip(-0.35, 0.35)
        residual_ret = _sector_neutral_returns(ret, sector_labels)

        bridge = _rolling_cross_sector_bridge(
            residual_ret=residual_ret,
            sector_labels=sector_labels,
            window=40,
            min_observations=20,
        )
        bridge_creation = bridge - bridge.shift(20)
        bridge_z = _trailing_zscore(bridge_creation, 50, 20).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        valid_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
        volume_base = valid_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        log_relative_volume = np.log(valid_volume / volume_base)
        volume_z = _trailing_zscore(log_relative_volume, 50, 20).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        # Both conditions must be elevated: a new diversified correlation bridge
        # and an unusually large participation shock.
        forced_flow_intensity = bridge_z.clip(lower=0.0) * volume_z.clip(lower=0.0)
        recent_residual_move = residual_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=2).sum()
        raw_signal = -recent_residual_move * forced_flow_intensity

        return rank(raw_signal).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.5)

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_standardized_innovation(
    values: pd.DataFrame, window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal innovation relative to a prior-only rolling liquidity regime."""
    history = values.shift(1)
    baseline = history.rolling(window, min_periods=max(8, window // 2)).mean()
    dispersion = history.rolling(window, min_periods=max(8, window // 2)).std()
    dispersion = dispersion.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (values - baseline) / dispersion


def _leave_one_out_sector_mean(
    values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute same-date leave-one-out sector means without deprecated axis grouping.

    Sector labels are forward-filled only, preserving point-in-time availability.
    A name with no available sector label, or no sector peer, receives NaN rather
    than being pooled into an artificial miscellaneous sector.
    """
    labels = sector.ffill()
    value_array = values.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    label_array = labels.to_numpy(dtype=object, copy=False)
    result = np.full(value_array.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)

    for row in range(value_array.shape[0]):
        row_values = value_array[row]
        row_labels = label_array[row]
        valid = np.isfinite(row_values) & ~pd.isna(row_labels)
        if not valid.any():
            continue

        for group in pd.unique(row_labels[valid]):
            members = valid & (row_labels == group)
            count = int(members.sum())
            if count > 1:
                total = row_values[members].sum()
                result[row, members] = (total - row_values[members]) / (count - 1)

    return pd.DataFrame(result, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)


@register_factor
class LiquidityResilienceSynchronyBreakHazard(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks idiosyncratic liquidity vacuums by close-location repair versus hazard."""

    factor_id = "liquidity_resilience_synchrony_break_hazard"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Liquidity Synchrony-Break Hazard"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Causal normalized range-per-volume innovations are stripped of their "
        "leave-one-out sector component. Positive idiosyncratic depth shocks "
        "are signed by close location and scaled by recent range expansion, "
        "ranking repaired strong closes above downside liquidity hazards."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        span = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0)
        safe_close = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        safe_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0, np.nan)

        normalized_range = span / safe_close
        illiquidity = normalized_range / safe_volume
        log_illiquidity = np.log(illiquidity.clip(lower=1e-16))
        log_illiquidity = log_illiquidity.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        innovation = _prior_standardized_innovation(log_illiquidity, 20)
        sector_innovation = _leave_one_out_sector_mean(innovation, sector)
        idiosyncratic_shock = innovation - sector_innovation

        close_location = (2.0 * (close - low) / span.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0)
        close_location = close_location.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        prior_range = normalized_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        range_state = np.log(normalized_range / prior_range.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        range_state = range_state.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(
            lower=-1.0, upper=1.0
        )
        expansion_scale = (1.0 + 0.5 * range_state.fillna(0.0)).clip(lower=0.25)

        positive_local_vacuum = idiosyncratic_shock.clip(lower=0.0)
        bounded_vacuum = np.tanh(positive_local_vacuum)
        score = bounded_vacuum * close_location * expansion_scale

        return rank(score).fillna(0.5)

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _quadratic_absorption_zscore(
    flow_size: pd.DataFrame,
    intrabar_range: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal quadratic impact residual: expected range minus realized range.

    A trailing quadratic regression estimates the normal concave/convex range
    response to directional flow magnitude.  Positive standardized residuals
    identify unusually muted realized impact, conditional on contemporaneous
    flow.  All moments use trailing windows ending at the current bar.
    """
    x = flow_size.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    y = intrabar_range.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    valid = x.notna() & y.notna()

    xv = x.where(valid)
    yv = y.where(valid)
    min_obs = max(20, window // 2)

    s0 = valid.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).sum()
    s1 = xv.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).sum()
    s2 = (xv * xv).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).sum()
    s3 = (xv * xv * xv).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).sum()
    s4 = (xv * xv * xv * xv).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).sum()
    sy = yv.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).sum()
    sxy = (xv * yv).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).sum()
    sx2y = (xv * xv * yv).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).sum()

    # Normal-equation inverse for y = b0 + b1*x + b2*x^2, implemented as
    # determinant ratios to retain full panel vectorisation.
    determinant = (
        s0 * (s2 * s4 - s3 * s3)
        - s1 * (s1 * s4 - s2 * s3)
        + s2 * (s1 * s3 - s2 * s2)
    )
    safe_det = determinant.where(determinant.abs() > 1e-12)

    b0 = (
        sy * (s2 * s4 - s3 * s3)
        - s1 * (sxy * s4 - s3 * sx2y)
        + s2 * (sxy * s3 - s2 * sx2y)
    ) / safe_det
    b1 = (
        s0 * (sxy * s4 - s3 * sx2y)
        - sy * (s1 * s4 - s2 * s3)
        + s2 * (s1 * sx2y - sxy * s2)
    ) / safe_det
    b2 = (
        s0 * (s2 * sx2y - sxy * s3)
        - s1 * (s1 * sx2y - sxy * s2)
        + sy * (s1 * s3 - s2 * s2)
    ) / safe_det

    expected = (b0 + b1 * xv + b2 * xv * xv).clip(lower=0.0)
    residual = yv - expected
    residual_scale = residual.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).std()
    muted_impact = (expected - yv) / residual_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return muted_impact.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _sector_pressure(
    pressure: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return same-sector mean directional pressure and a valid-peer mask."""
    labels = sector.ffill().bfill().iloc[-1].reindex(pressure.columns)
    labels = labels.astype(object)
    missing = labels.isna()
    if missing.any():
        labels.loc[missing] = ["__missing_sector_%d" % i for i in range(missing.sum())]

    counts = labels.value_counts(dropna=False)
    peer_count = labels.map(counts).astype(float)
    sector_mean = pressure.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T
    valid_peer = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to((peer_count >= 2).to_numpy(), pressure.shape),
        index=pressure.index,
        columns=pressure.columns,
    )
    return sector_mean, valid_peer


@register_factor
class SynchronizedImpactConvexityDirectionalRelease(BaseFactor):
    """Muted high-volume flow with broad same-sector directional confirmation."""

    factor_id = "synchronized_impact_convexity_directional_release"
    name = "Synchronized Absorption Release"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Estimates a trailing quadratic volume-to-range impact curve and longs "
        "(shorts) unusually absorbed buying (selling) when high-volume "
        "directional pressure is broad and aligned within the stock's sector."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].fillna(0.0)
        high = data["high"].where(data["high"].notna(), close)
        low = data["low"].where(data["low"].notna(), close)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        spread = high - low
        close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / spread.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        close_location = close_location.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        valid_prices = (high > 0.0) & (low > 0.0) & (high >= low)
        intrabar_range = np.log(high / low).where(valid_prices)

        average_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        relative_volume = volume / average_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_volume = relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=10.0)

        # Signed close-location flow gives buying/selling direction; its
        # magnitude rises smoothly with abnormal participation.
        signed_flow = close_location * np.log1p(relative_volume)
        flow_size = signed_flow.abs()
        muted_z = _quadratic_absorption_zscore(flow_size, intrabar_range, 60)

        # Restrict absorption to genuinely elevated participation rather than
        # quiet, naturally narrow bars.
        unusual_volume = (relative_volume - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        absorption = muted_z.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0) * unusual_volume

        # Each peer contributes only high-volume, close-location-signed flow.
        # The sector mean is a directional breadth measure rather than a market
        # aggregate: disagreement among peers cancels it out.
        peer_pressure = (
            np.sign(signed_flow)
            * close_location.abs()
            * unusual_volume
        ).fillna(0.0)
        sector_mean, has_peers = _sector_pressure(peer_pressure, data["sector"])

        own_direction = np.sign(signed_flow).fillna(0.0)
        aligned = (own_direction * sector_mean > 0.0).astype(float)
        directional_release = (
            own_direction
            * absorption.fillna(0.0)
            * sector_mean.abs().fillna(0.0)
            * aligned
        ).where(has_peers, 0.0)

        return rank(directional_release.fillna(0.0))

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_neutral_returns(
    close: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove each date's equal-weighted sector return using static labels."""
    ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    labels = sector.iloc[0].copy().fillna("Unknown").astype(str)
    sector_mean = ret.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T
    return (ret - sector_mean).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _correlation_bridge_score(
    neutral_ret: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, window: int, edges: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal rolling cross-sector correlation-bridge score.

    For each stock, the strongest cross-sector correlation edges are collected.
    Their correlation-weighted entropy across destination sectors measures whether
    the stock is synchronizing with multiple otherwise distinct communities.
    """
    n_rows, n_cols = neutral_ret.shape
    result = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    values = neutral_ret.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=True)
    sector_labels = labels.reindex(neutral_ret.columns).fillna("Unknown").astype(str)
    label_array = sector_labels.to_numpy(dtype=object, copy=True)
    total_sectors = max(int(pd.Series(label_array).nunique()), 1)

    for end in range(window - 1, n_rows):
        sample = values[end - window + 1 : end + 1, :]
        valid = np.isfinite(sample).all(axis=0)
        if int(valid.sum()) < 3:
            continue

        valid_idx = np.flatnonzero(valid)
        x = sample[:, valid_idx]
        x = x - x.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
        norms = np.sqrt(np.sum(x * x, axis=0))
        nonconstant = norms > 1.0e-12
        if int(nonconstant.sum()) < 3:
            continue

        idx = valid_idx[nonconstant]
        x = x[:, nonconstant]
        norms = norms[nonconstant]
        corr = (x.T @ x) / np.outer(norms, norms)
        corr = np.asarray(corr, dtype=float).copy()
        corr = np.clip(corr, -1.0, 1.0)
        np.fill_diagonal(corr, 0.0)

        current_labels = label_array[idx]
        for local_i, global_i in enumerate(idx):
            other_sector = current_labels != current_labels[local_i]
            candidate = np.flatnonzero(other_sector)
            if candidate.size == 0:
                result[end, global_i] = 0.0
                continue

            strength = np.abs(corr[local_i, candidate])
            finite = np.isfinite(strength) & (strength > 0.0)
            candidate = candidate[finite]
            strength = strength[finite]
            if candidate.size == 0:
                result[end, global_i] = 0.0
                continue

            take = min(edges, candidate.size)
            selected = np.argpartition(strength, -take)[-take:]
            neighbor_idx = candidate[selected]
            weights = strength[selected]
            weight_sum = float(weights.sum())
            if weight_sum <= 0.0:
                result[end, global_i] = 0.0
                continue

            neighbor_labels = current_labels[neighbor_idx]
            _, inverse = np.unique(neighbor_labels, return_inverse=True)
            sector_weight = np.bincount(inverse, weights=weights)
            probabilities = sector_weight / weight_sum
            entropy = -float(np.sum(probabilities * np.log(probabilities)))
            max_entropy = np.log(max(total_sectors - 1, 2))
            diversity = entropy / max_entropy
            mean_strength = float(weights.mean())
            result[end, global_i] = mean_strength * np.clip(diversity, 0.0, 1.0)

    return pd.DataFrame(result, index=neutral_ret.index, columns=neutral_ret.columns)


@register_factor
class CorrelationBridgeForcedFlowReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Fade sector-neutral moves accompanied by new cross-sector correlation bridges."""

    factor_id = "correlation_bridge_forcedflow_reversal"
    name = "Correlation-Bridge Forced-Flow Reversal"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Builds a trailing sector-neutral correlation graph and identifies stocks "
        "whose strongest cross-sector links become more diversified and intense. "
        "It fades large residual moves only when bridge creation and relative "
        "volume both indicate broad forced-flow synchronization."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        sector = data["sector"]

        neutral_ret = _sector_neutral_returns(close, sector)
        labels = sector.iloc[0].copy().fillna("Unknown").astype(str)
        bridge = _correlation_bridge_score(neutral_ret, labels, 50, 8)

        bridge_creation = (bridge - bridge.shift(10)).clip(lower=0.0)
        volume_base = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_volume_shock = (volume / volume_base - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)

        recent_residual_move = neutral_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=2).sum()
        activation = bridge_creation.fillna(0.0) * relative_volume_shock.fillna(0.0)
        raw_signal = -recent_residual_move.fillna(0.0) * activation
        return rank(raw_signal).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

Application of Deep Learning for Factor Timing in Asset Management

APPLICATION OF DEEP LEARNING FOR FACTOR TIMING IN ASSET MANAGEMENT 
Prabhu Prasad Panda, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, US 
Maysam Khodayari Gharanchaei, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, US 
Xilin Chen, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, US 
Haoshu Lyu, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, US 
 
ABSTRACT 
The p aper examines the performance of regression models (OLS linear regression, Ridge regression, 
Random Forest, and Fully -connected Neural Network) on the prediction of CMA (Conservative Minus 
Aggressive) factor premium and the performance of factor timing investm ent with them. Out-of-sample R-
squared shows that more flexible models have better performance in explaining the variance in factor 
premium of the unseen period, and the back testing affirms that the factor timing based on more flexible 
models tends to over perform the ones with linear models. However, for flexible models like neural networks, 
the optimal weights based on their prediction tend to be unstable, which can lead to high transaction costs 
and market impacts. We verify that tilting down the rebalance frequency according to the historical optimal 
rebalancing scheme can help reduce the transaction costs. 
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning, Factor Timing, Asset Management 
1. INTRODUCTION 
The practicality of timing factor investments remains a hotly debated topic in the financial world. A primary 
point of contention centres on the ability to predict factor premiums  (Agrawal et al., 1992), which is crucial 
for successful factor timing (Black et al., 1972). However, (Asness, 2017) reveals that numerous traditional 
macroeconomic and fundamental variables lack significant explanatory power in a longer time frame and 
the timing is hard to implement. The current situation of factor timing research resembles the equity 
premium prediction (Basu, 1983) and (Bhandari, 1988) back in past, where adjustments to existing models 
and new models are introduced. Here we hope to see whether they will also help the exploration of factor 
timing. 
 
2. DATA 
We source our factor data from Fama and French  (Breeden, 1979), accessible at Kenneth French ’s data 
library (Breeden et al., 1989) (monthly, January 1963 to December 2022), and our timing variable data from 
Welch and Goyal (2008), accessible at Goyal’s website (Campbell and Thompson, 2008) (monthly, January 
1871 to December 2022). We merge these 2 datasets, and the merged table comprises 714 months of 
values for factors and timing variables from July 1963 to December 2022 (around 60 years). We choose to 
time the Conservative Minus Aggre ssive (CMA) factor with Term spread (tms, which reflects the interest 
rate macro) and Default spread (Chan et al., 1985) (dfy, which reflects the prevailing credit condition) of the 
previous month from Welch and Goyal (2008), together its own 1 -month lag (which handles the 
autocorrelation). As for training -testing split, we choose to use 1963 -2002 as the training period (474 
months) and 2003 -2022 as the testing perio d (240 months). The data is of monthly frequency (more 
specifically, end-of-month). 

 
3. METHODS 
3.1 Predictive Models for Factor Premium 
To compute the factor-timing weights of the CMA factor, we need the conditional expected premium E[rt+1] 
of the factor (Chan et al., 1985) , we start with a predictor f that predicts the factor premium (Chan et al., 
1985) with the features xt:

To reflect the nature of prediction and model calibration, all models other than NN3 are fitted in an expanding
